decided: Supersedes the earlier shard on this branch, whose mechanism and scope review proved wrong. The trigger still moves to the wave-3 `cmd/shortfall/v*` tag, but NOT via goreleaser's `monorepo.tag_prefix` — that field is Pro-only and the pinned OSS v2.18.0 rejects the config outright. The version is instead handed over as GORELEASER_CURRENT_TAG by a guard script, and goreleaser runs with --skip=validate. A release is two commits, not one: the release commit bumps the seventeen replaced modules' requires and carries tag waves 1-2; a second commit bumps cmd/shortfall's three requires and tidies its go.sum, and carries wave 3, which triggers the release. Founder chose this shape over two alternatives on 2026-09-01 after the cost was re-presented.
why: Three facts, each established empirically this session, forced the shape. (1) A require in cmd/shortfall is really resolved now that it has no replace, so naming a not-yet-tagged version does not merely skew a check — it fails the build of EVERY module in the workspace, because go.work computes one module graph: ./scripts/ci-go.sh build goes red for biz, registry and emit on a commit that has not been tagged. So the CLI cannot be bumped before its dependencies are published, while the seventeen replaced modules can and must be, so that each one's published go.mod names the release it ships in. (2) cmd/shortfall/go.sum cannot gain a version's hashes before that version is fetchable — go mod tidy says 'unknown revision' and no flag invents them — so the tidy is necessarily a second commit. Adopters are unaffected either way: go install pkg@version does not consult the target module's go.sum, verified by installing a module whose go.sum carried no first-party hashes at all. (3) goreleaser's git pipe runs `git describe --exact-match --tags --match $GORELEASER_CURRENT_TAG` at HEAD, so naming the root tag demands it sit at HEAD — which (1) and (2) make impossible. --skip=validate is what reconciles them, and it is a consequence of the shape rather than a relaxation of it.
cost_if_wrong: The release ritual is now two PRs per version instead of one, and it is order-dependent in a way a hurried operator can get wrong. That cost is paid down rather than documented away: scripts/release-guard.sh refuses to build unless the CLI carries no replace, every first-party require names the version being released, and each one's tag exists and is reachable from the commit being built — and scripts/release-guard-test.sh drives all fifteen of those branches in CI, because a check standing between a tag and published binaries should not be shell that nothing exercises. --skip=validate costs three goreleaser checks and each is made elsewhere: tag-at-HEAD replaced by the guard's existence-and-reachability check, clean-tree asserted with the same `git status --porcelain` goreleaser uses, and semver — which that flag downgrades to a warning, leaving `prerelease: auto` silently inert — rejected by the guard outright. The residual risk is a skipped wave producing no release at all: a loud, self-announcing failure, which is the direction to fail in.
alternatives: CLI lags one library version — cmd/shortfall permanently requires the previous release's modules, so nothing is ever unpublished, the trigger stays on the root tag and no goreleaser check is skipped. Rejected by the founder: it trades a one-time process cost for a permanent, user-visible oddity, where `shortfall v0.3.0` is built on the v0.2.0 library forever.

Revert to keeping the replaces and close the item as a recorded no — zero release risk, but the idiomatic install path stays broken on a public repo. Rejected: the two facts that justified it (private repo, nothing published) both expired.

goreleaser `monorepo: tag_prefix` — the original shard's mechanism. Rejected because it does not exist in the pinned build: `goreleaser check` on v2.18.0 reports 'field monorepo not found in type config.Project'.

Let goreleaser build through go.work instead of published modules — rejected: it contradicts the stated reason for GOWORK=off, and it would ship a binary built from the tree while `go install` gives adopters one built from published tags, so the two would silently diverge.
scope: Wider than the first shard claimed, and this is the correction: .github/workflows/release.yml gains the guard invocation, a clean-tree assertion, --skip=validate and a snapshot version fix (the rehearsal was deriving its version from `git describe`, which returns an adapter tag here, producing archives named as nested directories); .github/workflows/ci.yml gains a release-guard regression job, NOT in the required set — making it required is a branch-protection change only the founder can make; scripts/release-guard.sh and scripts/release-guard-test.sh are new; cmd/shortfall/go.mod and go.sum drop the replaces; test/modgraph gains OtherReplaces, the no-replace-at-all rule for install targets, and the version-agreement narrowing with a non-vacuity floor; and README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/quickstart.md and docs/internal/go-public-checklist.md state the new truth. Gate surface is in scope because workspace-47f's acceptance criteria is explicitly about the release pipeline, which .warden/skills-policy.md 'Forbidden paths' permits for a tracked item about CI, stated in the PR body. No change to the CLI's source or to any library module.
